description: A programmable sequencer in the manner of the Roland MC-4. A sequence is built stage by stage, and finished sequences are stored as patterns that can be played one after another

params.text: Returns the sequencer to its first stage
The rate of the internal clock
Switches pattern playing on and off, so the stored patterns are played one after another rather than the single sequence

inputs.text: A trigger starts and stops the sequencer
A clock here takes over from the internal clock
A pulse resets the phase of the internal clock, to bring it into step with something else

outputs.text: The note of the stage being played, as a pitch voltage
The second voltage of the stage being played
Sends a pulse on each stage
A gate on each stage, as long as that stage's gate setting makes it
Passes on the clock the sequencer is running on
Sends a pulse each time the sequencer is reset
Sends a pulse when a pattern reaches its end

notes: each stage carries a note, a second voltage, a gate length and a length of its own
NUM STAGES shows how many stages the sequence holds, and CURR STAGE is clicked to choose which stage the displays below it show
NOTE sets the pitch the CV1 output carries for that stage, and can be set to REST for a silent stage
CV2 sets the second voltage that stage carries
GATE sets how much of that stage's length the gate output stays high for, as a percentage
LENGTH sets how long that stage lasts, from 1/384 to 1/12 of a note, 1/16 to begin with
NUM PATTERNS shows how many patterns are stored and CURR PATTERN is clicked to choose which one is loaded
a new sequencer holds no stages and plays nothing: set the note, second voltage, gate and length on the displays, then add a stage with ADD STAGE, and repeat for each stage of the sequence.
a sequence is stored as a pattern with ADD PATTERN, and pattern playing steps through the stored patterns one after another rather than the sequence being edited.
with the mouse over the module the number keys type a value, and N chooses note entry, D length, G gate and C or V the second voltage
with the mouse over the module, R sets the note to REST, keypad Enter adds a stage at the end, Return updates the current stage and I inserts one before it
with the mouse over the module, Page Up and Page Down move between stages and Escape drops the edits to the current stage
menu: SHOW RUNNING STAGE — keeps the displays following the stage and pattern being played
CONTINUOUS EDIT — writes each edit into the current stage as it is made, while the sequencer is stopped
TRANSPOSE — moves the whole sequence with TRANSPOSE +12, TRANSPOSE +1, TRANSPOSE -1 and TRANSPOSE -12
TRANSPOSE PATTERN +12 — moves the current pattern up an octave, with TRANSPOSE PATTERN +1, TRANSPOSE PATTERN -1 and TRANSPOSE PATTERN -12 beside it
STAGE COMMANDS — ADD STAGE, INSERT STAGE, UPDATE CURR STAGE FROM SCREEN, LOAD CURR STAGE TO SCREEN and DELETE STAGE, all acting on the sequence being edited
PATTERN COMMANDS — ADD PATTERN, INSERT PATTERN, UPDATE CURR PATTERN FROM SEQUENCE and LOAD PATTERN TO SEQUENCE, all acting on the stored patterns
EDIT — COPY SEQUENCE, CUT SEQUENCE, PASTE SEQUENCE and DELETE SEQUENCE act on a whole sequence
COPY CURR PATTERN — with CUT CURR PATTERN, PASTE PATTERN, DELETE CURR PATTERN and DELETE ALL PATTERNS, acts on the stored patterns
DELETE SEQUENCE — printed with (option/window key down) and carried out only with that key held, as is DELETE ALL PATTERNS
